turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so I'll be direct. Owen found out about a zero from the gradebook on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me. Who decided that, and on what basis?
"Get this over with." Then answer me. Did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?
Look, your son cheated. Everyone knows it. I'm not wasting my evening on this.
My child never lies. "Everyone knows it" isn't evidence, Hale, and I'm writing down that you said it. What do you actually have, or am I going to the principal's office?
You lawyers think you can bully anyone.
I'm asking for a document, Hale, not bullying you. Your own procedure says a parent is called before any mark goes in, and nobody called me. Take the zero off, or show me what you have.
Are you going to keep wasting my time?
You asked for this meeting, Hale. I'm the one with a call at 4:40. Put something with a date on it in front of me, or I'm going to the principal.
